title: The Wanderer
author: Anonymous
source_notes: Old English text from the Exeter Book (late 10th c.). Translation by R. K. Gordon, 'Anglo-Saxon Poetry' (1926). Edition following the Klaeber/Krapp-Dobbie tradition.
reading_notes: The Wanderer is the most famous Old English elegy. A lone exile, his lord dead, his kinsmen scattered, speaks of memory, solitude, and the passing of all worldly glory. The poem moves from a personal lament into a universal meditation on mutability, ending with a Christian frame. Its closing question, 'Hwær cwom mearg? Hwær cwom mago?' ('Where is the horse? where the rider?') echoes through medieval poetry and was famously reworked by Tolkien.

lines.original: Oft him anhaga are gebideð,
lines.english: Often the solitary one finds grace for himself,
lines.gloss: Oft = 'often'; him = 'for himself' (reflexive dative); anhaga = 'solitary one, lone-dweller' (nominative, compound an + haga); are = 'grace, favor' (accusative); gebideð = 'awaits, experiences' (3rd singular of gebidan).

lines.original: metudes miltse, þeah þe he modcearig
lines.english: the mercy of the Lord, though he, sorrowful of heart,
lines.gloss: metudes = 'of the Creator' (genitive of metod); miltse = 'mercy' (accusative of milts); þeah þe = 'although' (conj.); he = 'he'; modcearig = 'sorrowful in mind' (compound mod + cearig, nominative).

lines.original: geond lagulade longe sceolde
lines.english: across the water-way has long had to
lines.gloss: geond = 'across, throughout' (prep. + accusative); lagulade = 'water-way, sea-path' (accusative; kenning); longe = 'long' (adverb); sceolde = 'had to, must' (past of sculan).

lines.original: hreran mid hondum hrimcealde sæ,
lines.english: stir with his hands the ice-cold sea,
lines.gloss: hreran = 'to stir, move' (infinitive); mid hondum = 'with hands' (dative plural); hrimcealde = 'frost-cold' (accusative, compound); sæ = 'sea' (accusative).

lines.original: wadan wræclastas. Wyrd bið ful aræd!
lines.english: tread the paths of exile. Fate is full fixed!
lines.gloss: wadan = 'to go, tread' (infinitive); wræclastas = 'exile-paths, tracks of exile' (accusative plural, compound wræc + last); Wyrd = 'fate, what happens' (nominative); bið = 'is' (habitual); ful aræd = 'fully fixed, determined'.

lines.original: Swa cwæð eardstapa, earfeþa gemyndig,
lines.english: So spoke the wanderer, mindful of hardships,
lines.gloss: Swa = 'thus'; cwæð = 'spoke' (past of cweðan); eardstapa = 'earth-stepper, wanderer' (nominative; kenning); earfeþa = 'of hardships' (genitive plural); gemyndig = 'mindful' (nominative + genitive object).

lines.original: wraþra wælsleahta, winemæga hryres:
lines.english: of fierce slaughters, the fall of dear kinsmen:
lines.gloss: wraþra = 'of cruel, fierce' (genitive plural); wælsleahta = 'of slaughters' (genitive plural, compound wæl + sleaht); winemæga = 'of beloved kinsmen' (genitive plural, compound wine + mæg); hryres = 'of fall, ruin' (genitive).

lines.original: "Oft ic sceolde ana uhtna gehwylce
lines.english: "Often I have had to alone at each dawn
lines.gloss: Oft = 'often'; ic = 'I'; sceolde = 'had to' (past of sculan); ana = 'alone' (nominative singular); uhtna = 'of dawns' (genitive plural); gehwylce = 'at each' (dative, distributive).

lines.original: mine ceare cwiþan. Nis nu cwicra nan
lines.english: lament my sorrow. There is now none living
lines.gloss: mine = 'my' (accusative); ceare = 'sorrow, care' (accusative); cwiþan = 'to lament' (infinitive); Nis = 'is not' (ne + is); nu = 'now'; cwicra = 'of the living' (genitive plural); nan = 'none' (nominative).

lines.original: þe ic him modsefan minne durre
lines.english: to whom I would dare to tell my inmost thought,
lines.gloss: þe = 'to whom' (relative); ic = 'I'; him = 'to him' (dative); modsefan = 'mind, spirit' (accusative of modsefa); minne = 'my' (accusative masculine); durre = 'dare' (subjunctive of durran).

lines.original: sweotule asecgan. Ic to soþe wat
lines.english: openly speak. I know for truth
lines.gloss: sweotule = 'clearly, openly' (adverb); asecgan = 'to speak out' (infinitive); Ic = 'I'; to soþe = 'for truth' (prep. + dative); wat = 'know' (1st singular of witan).

lines.original: þæt biþ in eorle indryhten þeaw,
lines.english: that it is a noble custom in a man
lines.gloss: þæt = 'that'; biþ = 'is'; in eorle = 'in a man' (dative); indryhten = 'noble' (nominative adjective); þeaw = 'custom, habit' (nominative).

lines.original: þæt he his ferðlocan fæste binde,
lines.english: to bind fast his spirit-chamber,
lines.gloss: þæt = 'that'; he = 'he'; his = 'his'; ferðlocan = 'mind-enclosure, breast' (accusative compound kenning); fæste = 'firmly' (adverb); binde = 'bind' (subjunctive of bindan).

lines.original: healde his hordcofan, hycge swa he wille.
lines.english: keep his treasure-chamber, think as he will.
lines.gloss: healde = 'keep' (subjunctive); hordcofan = 'treasure-chamber' (accusative, metaphor for heart); hycge = 'think' (subjunctive of hycgan); swa he wille = 'as he will'.

lines.original: Ne mæg werig mod wyrde wiðstondan,
lines.english: The weary mind cannot withstand fate,
lines.gloss: Ne mæg = 'cannot' (ne + mæg); werig = 'weary' (nominative); mod = 'mind, heart' (nominative); wyrde = 'fate' (dative object of withstond); wiðstondan = 'to withstand' (infinitive + dative).

lines.original: ne se hreo hyge helpe gefremman.
lines.english: nor the troubled heart bring help.
lines.gloss: ne = 'nor'; se = 'the' (nominative masculine); hreo = 'troubled, stormy' (nominative); hyge = 'heart, mind' (nominative); helpe = 'help' (accusative); gefremman = 'to bring about' (infinitive).

lines.original: Forðon domgeorne dreorigne oft
lines.english: Therefore those eager for glory often
lines.gloss: Forðon = 'therefore'; domgeorne = 'eager for glory' (nominative plural, compound dom + georn); dreorigne = 'sad, dreary' (accusative masculine); oft = 'often'.

lines.original: in hyra breostcofan bindað fæste;
lines.english: bind fast in their breast-chamber (a sorrowful thought);
lines.gloss: in hyra = 'in their' (dative); breostcofan = 'breast-chamber' (dative singular compound); bindað = 'bind' (3rd plural of bindan); fæste = 'firmly'.

lines.original: swa ic modsefan minne sceolde,
lines.english: so have I, too, had to bind my mind,
lines.gloss: swa = 'so'; ic = 'I'; modsefan = 'spirit' (accusative); minne = 'my' (accusative); sceolde = 'had to' (past of sculan).

lines.original: oft earmcearig, eðle bidæled,
lines.english: often wretched, deprived of my homeland,
lines.gloss: oft = 'often'; earmcearig = 'wretchedly sorrowful' (nominative compound); eðle = 'from homeland' (dative of separation); bidæled = 'deprived' (past participle + dative).

lines.original: freomægum feor feterum sælan,
lines.english: far from noble kinsmen, fasten it in fetters,
lines.gloss: freomægum = 'from noble kinsmen' (dative plural compound); feor = 'far'; feterum = 'with fetters' (dative plural); sælan = 'to bind' (infinitive).

lines.original: siþþan geara iu goldwine minne
lines.english: since long years ago my lord of gold
lines.gloss: siþþan = 'since'; geara iu = 'long ago' (idiom); goldwine = 'gold-friend, lord' (accusative singular compound kenning); minne = 'my' (accusative masculine).

lines.original: hrusan heolstre biwrah, ond ic hean þonan
lines.english: earth's darkness enwrapped, and I, abject, thence
lines.gloss: hrusan = 'of earth' (dative); heolstre = 'with darkness, shadow' (dative); biwrah = 'covered, enwrapped' (past of bewreon); ond = 'and'; ic = 'I'; hean = 'humbled, abject' (nominative); þonan = 'thence, from there'.

lines.original: wod wintercearig ofer waþema gebind,
lines.english: went, winter-desolate, over the waves' binding,
lines.gloss: wod = 'went, waded' (past of wadan); wintercearig = 'winter-sorrowful' (nominative compound); ofer = 'over' (+accusative); waþema = 'of waves' (genitive plural); gebind = 'binding, expanse' (accusative).

lines.original: sohte sele dreorig sinces bryttan,
lines.english: dreary sought the hall of a giver of treasure,
lines.gloss: sohte = 'sought' (past of secan); sele = 'hall' (accusative); dreorig = 'sad'; sinces = 'of treasure' (genitive); bryttan = 'of a dispenser, giver' (genitive of brytta).

lines.original: hwær ic feor oþþe neah findan meahte
lines.english: where far or near I might find
lines.gloss: hwær = 'where'; ic = 'I'; feor = 'far'; oþþe = 'or'; neah = 'near'; findan = 'to find' (infinitive); meahte = 'might' (past of magan).

lines.original: þone þe in meoduhealle min mine wisse,
lines.english: one who in the mead-hall might know my own,
lines.gloss: þone = 'him' (accusative demonstrative); þe = 'who' (relative); in meoduhealle = 'in the mead-hall' (dative singular compound); min mine wisse = 'who might know mine' (archaic, with genitive; idiomatic 'know my affairs').

lines.original: oþþe mec freondleasne frefran wolde,
lines.english: or who would comfort me, friendless,
lines.gloss: oþþe = 'or'; mec = 'me' (accusative); freondleasne = 'friendless' (accusative masculine); frefran = 'to comfort' (infinitive); wolde = 'would' (past of willan).

lines.original: wenian mid wynnum. Wat se þe cunnað
lines.english: treat me with joys. He knows, who has tried,
lines.gloss: wenian = 'to entertain, treat' (infinitive); mid wynnum = 'with joys' (dative plural); Wat = 'knows' (3rd singular of witan); se þe = 'he who' (relative); cunnað = 'tries, experiences' (3rd singular of cunnian).

sections.title: Where Are They Gone? (lines 92-96 — the famous 'ubi sunt' passage)

lines.original: Hwær cwom mearg? Hwær cwom mago? Hwær cwom maþþumgyfa?
lines.english: Where is the horse gone? where the rider? where the giver of treasure?
lines.gloss: Hwær = 'where'; cwom = 'came, has gone' (past of cuman, idiom for 'is now'); mearg = 'horse' (nominative); mago = 'young man, warrior' (nominative); maþþumgyfa = 'treasure-giver' (nominative compound).

lines.original: Hwær cwom symbla gesetu? Hwær sindon seledreamas?
lines.english: Where are the feast-seats? where are the hall-joys?
lines.gloss: Hwær = 'where'; cwom = 'has gone'; symbla = 'of feasts' (genitive plural); gesetu = 'seats' (nominative plural); sindon = 'are' (3rd plural of beon); seledreamas = 'hall-joys' (nominative plural compound).

lines.original: Eala beorht bune! Eala byrnwiga!
lines.english: Alas, the bright cup! alas, the mailed warrior!
lines.gloss: Eala = 'Alas!' (interjection); beorht = 'bright'; bune = 'cup, drinking vessel' (nominative singular, vocative exclamation); byrnwiga = 'mailed warrior' (nominative compound).

lines.original: Eala þeodnes þrym! Hu seo þrag gewat,
lines.english: Alas, the glory of the prince! How that time has passed,
lines.gloss: Eala = 'Alas'; þeodnes = 'of the prince' (genitive); þrym = 'glory' (nominative); Hu = 'how'; seo = 'that' (feminine); þrag = 'time, period' (nominative); gewat = 'has departed' (past of gewitan).

lines.original: genap under nihthelm, swa heo no wære.
lines.english: darkened under the helm of night, as if it had never been.
lines.gloss: genap = 'grew dark' (past of genipan); under = 'under' (+dative); nihthelm = 'helm of night, darkness' (dative singular compound); swa = 'as if'; heo = 'it' (referring to þrag); no wære = 'had not been' (subjunctive, negative).
